newsitem.title: UK: London freight - Rates fall despite panamax reviva.
newsitem.headline: London freight - Rates fall despite panamax reviva.

text.p: London, April 15 (REUTER) - In spite of a revival of activity in panamax grain chartering from U.S. Gulf for first half May and evidence of some strenthening of demand for capers in the Atlantic, freight rates have continued to fall more or less worldwide, brokers said.

The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) dropped another nine points to 1,411, while the decline was less marked for handysizes, which was reflected in the Baltic Handy Index, at 1,097, down two points from Monday.
GRAIN - Brokers reported that panamax tonnage was ballasting in numbers in both the Atlantic and the Far East.
South Korean charterers were said to be now quoting voyage rates instead of timecharter for Nopac grain to South Korea and Taiwan.
The weak panamax market was expected to lead to more vessels open in the East to consider loading in the Atlantic, but rates were also softening in that area.
The revival of chartering from U.S. Gulf for first half May was welcome to owners but the levels in the critical U.S. Gulf/Japan trade have once again eased.
NYK was said to have booked Baumare II for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain at $23.75 no combo for early May.
This was the same as agreed by Keoyang yesterday. (Baumare II failed with Transfield for a Tampa/China trip with fertilizers), brokers said.

Hanjin declined Oldendorff tonnage on the same position at $23.60 and fixed instead Maritime Grace at $23.50. Continental was reported to have booked Kardamyla for 52,000 tonnes heavy grain for early May also at $23.50 no combo.
Reports that Halla fixed Joy Sea in this trade for April 25/May 5 loading could not be verified.
In the swaps market, May was trading at a 50 cents premium to $24.00 combo.
Some traders reported seeing delayed U.S. Gulf cargoes rolling in to next month, others believed that the slippery slope into the summer months had already been reached.
Chartering business concluded from Argentina and Brazil was difficult to trace, brokers said.
Talk circulating the market suggested Interbulk fixed New Wave 52,000 dwt Brazil/Continent for end April, but no confirmation was forthcoming.
Finagrain fixed Alexia 58,412 dwt spot Vitoria, and New Spirit 52,000 dwt was booked up River Plate and Brazil to Italy, but details proved elusive.

Cabral was said to have relet Minoan Sky 54,000 dwt open prompt Paranagua from the Mississippi, while Dreyfus fixed Cosmar for 35,000 tonnes grains at a lumpsum equivalent of only $16.00 basis 1-2 to France and Spain, and Cargill covered 50,000 tonnes barley Vancouver/Saudi Arabia on private terms.
Few new orders were quoted but Cargill have another 25,000 tonnes wheat stem Rouen/Algeria for April/May, and 9,000 sunflower seeds stowing La Pallice/Casablanca for April 21/25.
MINERALS - Some owners/brokers were frustrated at the caper market which they thought should be rising but which was instead characterised by reports of weaker fixtures.
In the atlantic, Rohstoffhandel for example, fixed Veni for 150,000 tonnes iron ore Narvik/Rotterdam for May at $2.70 option loading Tubarao at $5.50.
China Steel booked unnamed Far Eastern controlled tonnage for 120,000 tonnes iron ore Brazil/Kaohsiung at a modest $9.20 for May/June option Sepetiba at $9.50.
In the Far East, British Steel took the Korea Line relet Anangel Splendour 161,643 dwt delivery China for a trip via Cape Lambert with iron ore to Redcar at an economical $14,250 daily.
Panamax levels also fell in the East, as indicated by the Showa fixture of Capitano Giovanni 75,000 dwt with coal.
Delivery was set for Japan April 22/25 for an east Australian coal round trip at $11,500 daily, down about $500 from the last similar fixture.
Some brokers suggested that HMM's fixture of Pacific Orient 67,478 dwt delivery Japan April 18/24 for 12 months trading at $10,300 daily might fail on subjects.
Cosco and Sinotrans were reported to be interested in similar tonnage for three to five months at about $11,000 to $11,250 daily.
At the close, BIFFEX futures were 15 to 45 points down. Most active April traded last at 1,365. Volume toalled 253 lots.
